Supplemental
Silvicom Inc Driver Policy and Driver Rules

In order to provide a consistent and professional driving force, Silvicom inc has promulgated the following rules for driver behavior and compensation. These rules can be changed from time to time By Silvicom Inc and copies shall be distributed to all drivers by email or fax or mail. The driver's signature on this policy statement indicated that driver is aware of these rules and agrees to these rules. these rules are in additional to rules and policies delineated in Silvicom Safety Standards and Policies attached hereto and made a part hereof.

1)  All mileage  shall be determined by computations provided by mileage provided by the program PC Miler. Said mileage shall be shown on settlement statement forwarded to Independent contractor/Driver either through email or mail.

The independent Contractor/Driver shall have 14 days after receipt of said mileage determination to file any objections in writing to carrier. Said objection shall explain any special circumstance that would render the computation of PC Miler inaccurate. The mileage as determined by PC Miler shall be presumed correct, but Carrier will consider any claim based upon emergency road conditions or detours.

With in 14 days of receipt of Independent Contractor's/Driver’s objection Carrier shall deliver a written reply either indicating any adjustments that will be made. The finding of Carrier shall be final.
2) Empty miles from last delivery to drivers home time city are not paid and deducted from his next empty/loaded miles when he returns to duty/dispatch/driving.

3) Due to possible charges, fines and claims last settlement with driver to be paid no later than 45 days from independent contractor/driver leaving Silvicom service.  Possible charges and offsets to include but not be limited to , equipment damage, unpaid tolls, duty violations and wear and tear on trailers(if applicable).
4) From time to time at drivers/Independent Contractor's request, Silvicom may advance funds to Driver/ Independent Contractor. There shall be a minimum $ 5.00 transaction fee for each advance.

5) If driver/independent contractor loses or misplaces bill of lading, driver/independent contractor next settlement shall not reflect those miles until Silvicom is paid by broker. Silvicom shall use its best efforts to seek payment form broker and Driver/Independent Contractor shall cooperate in providing documents required.

6) it is important for Silvicom to have proper receipts for accounting purposes. Therefore, any missing or lost fuel or expense receipts shall be charged to Driver/Independent Contractor on settlement at he rate of $10.00 per missing receipt.
7) Any lumper fee not reported to Silvicom within 24 hours of lumper service shall be responsibility of driver/ independent contractor.

8) Drivers/ Independent Contractors using Silvicom credit to purchase fuel, shall purchase fuel only once within 24 hour period. The second transaction shall be charged to driver at settlement. Silvicom reserves the right to waive this charge and authorize a second fueling, but driver/independent contractor must obtain Silvicom's written or texted approval for each additional purchase during that 24 hour period.
9) Without Silvicom approval truck and/or trailer wash done more than 50 miles from Silvicom corporate headquarters will be at Driver's/Independent Contractor's expense.

10) Driver/Independent Contractor shall be responsible for daily truck preventative maintenance.  Maintenance to include but not be limited to daily tire check to 100psi, daily check of all fluids (including wiper fluids), monitor mileage and notify Silvicom's equipment for oil changes every 35 thousand miles. Failure to maintain and check vehicles shall result in minimum  $100 per each occurrence. However, upon proof that damage to equipment or cargo is directly related to Driver/Independent Contractor failure to perform said periodic check, Driver/Independent Contractor shall be responsible for all consequential damages.
11) Silvicom shall be responsible for all tolls for it’s own vehicles, however, Driver/Independent Contractor to be responsible for all toll violations.

12) If Driver/Independent Contractor is using Silvicom 's equipment, at the end of Driver's/Independent Contractor’s relationship with Silvicom, Driver/Independent Contractor shall be responsible for return of the equipment in proper working order and undamaged ( normal wear and tear excepted) to Silvicom’ s corporate headquarters in Melrose Park, IL. If the equipment is not returned to Silvicom’ s corporate headquarters within  3 days of termination of Driver/Independent Contractor/Silvicom relationship, Driver/Independent Contractor shall be responsible for all costs to return said equipment to the corporate headquarters including but not  limited to substitute driver/independent contractor, fuel and towing if necessary.
13) Driver/Independent Contractor shall be responsible for all non-mechanical towing expenses.

14) Arbitration. All claims and disputes arising  under or relating to any agreement between Silvicom and Driver/Independent Contractor are to be settled by binding arbitration in the state of Illinois or another location mutually agreeable to the parties. The arbitration shall be conducted on  a confidential  basis pursuant to the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association. Any decision or award as a result of any such arbitration proceeding shall be in writing and shall provide an explanation for all conclusions of law and fact and shall include the assessment of costs, expenses. and reasonable attorney's fees . Any such arbitration shall be conducted by an arbitrator experienced in Interstate Commerce, trucking and independent contractor law and shall include a written record of the arbitration hearing. The parties reserve the right to object to any individual who shall be employed by or affiliated with a competing organization or entity. An award of arbitration may be confirmed in a court of competent jurisdiction.

15) All contracts between Silvicom and Independent Contractor/Driver shall be governed by the laws to  the State of Illinois. Also, any question specifically related to the status of Driver as Independent  Contractor shall be determined by the laws of the state of Illinois and not other jurisdiction.

16) Silvicom will be responsible for recruiting expense for flight ticket and hotel, or rental vehicle previously agreed on, unless driver leaves the company in the first 3 months from hire date. In which case, those expenses will be responsibility of the driver .

17) Drivers and/or Independent contractors are not allowed to reach out to broker/shipper/receiver  by themselves. All communication will be conducted thru Silvicom’ s dispatchers. Driver and/or Independent contractor will answer broker’s calls and inform Silvicom’ s dispatcher about it, but they are not allowed to contact individual brokers/shippers/receivers  and/or their corporate office first. All questions and concerns about loads should be addressed to Silvicom’ s dispatch team

18. Silvicom is not liable or responsible for drivers/independent contractors personal items in assigned truck. Please clear your belongings when truck is left for service and/or home time period especially.
Hours of Service Policy
Effective November 20th, 2013
Hours of service Requirements are detailed in CFR 49 Part 395 of FMCSA. Those regulations were written to reduce accidents/injuries due to driver fatigue. The Rules are as follow:
11 HOUR RULE
: You can not drive again until you have completed a 10 hour break after driving 11 hours since you last 10 hour break
14 HOUR RULE:
You cannot drive again until you have completed a 10 hour break after being on duty for 14 hours since your last 10 hour break.
60 HOUR RULE:
You cannot drive again until you have hours available after having been on duty 60 hours in the past 7 days-to be able to be on duty again you have to be off duty for at least 34  consecutive hours.
70 HOUR RULE:
You cannot drive again until you have hours available after having been on duty 70 hours in the past 8 days-to be able to be on duty again you have to be off duty for at least 34  consecutive hours.
FLASIFICATION :
You cannot falsify your log books or hide hours of service violation. All fuel receipts as well as any other documents with a date or time will be checked against logs for accuracy.

Personal conveyance would be acceptable when a driver is looking for a safe place to park after shift in case A) He/she is over hours and must leave shipper/receiver and/or B) Driver is running out of hours  and is stuck in the traffic C)  Truck stop is full and there is no parking space there. This includes traveling closer to the final load destination if that location is the closest, most reasonable safe location. But be advised that drivers can't use personal conveyance to  A) move a load closer to where it needs to be by bypassing available locations to park, B)bobtail or operate an empty trailer to retrieve another load or C)reposition a CMV or transport it to a maintenance facility. So the driver must enter note on ELD confirming that they did not bypass ANY available parking location and provide proof(receipts, driver written statement or text, shipper's/receiver's written statement, or police note/statement including police officer's info)
